content: Dimenhydrinate is an antiemetic medication that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of symptoms associated with motion sickness, including nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. Common side effects of this medication include nausea, vomiting, dry mouth (xerostomia), and sedation. Adult Indications and Dosage Indications: Dimenhydrinate is used to prevent and treat symptoms of motion sickness, such as nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. Dosage: To prevent motion sickness, the first dose should be taken 30 minutes to 1 hour before starting the activity. For prevention or treatment of motion sickness, follow the recommended dosing instructions. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Indications: Dimenhydrinate is used in children for the prevention and treatment of motion sickness symptoms, including nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. It should not be used in children under 2 years of age unless directed by a doctor. Dosage: Follow the specific dosing instructions for pediatric patients. Contraindications There are no specific contraindications listed for dimenhydrinate. Warnings and Precautions Ask a doctor before use if you have: A breathing problem such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis. Glaucoma. Difficulty urinating due to an enlarged prostate gland. Adverse Reactions Clinical Trials Experience: Marked drowsiness may occur when using this product. Alcohol, sedatives, and tranquilizers may increase drowsiness. Avoid alcoholic drinks. Exercise caution when driving a motor vehicle or operating machinery. Postmarketing Experience: There is limited information available regarding postmarketing experience with dimenhydrinate. Drug Interactions Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking: Sedatives or tranquilizers. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. There is no specific guidance from the Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) on the use of dimenhydrinate in pregnant women. Labor and Delivery: There is no FDA guidance on the use of dimenhydrinate during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: If breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. Pediatric Use: There is no FDA guidance on the use of dimenhydrinate in pediatric settings. Geriatric Use: There is no FDA guidance on the use of dimenhydrinate in geriatric populations. Gender, Race, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment, and Immunocompromised Patients: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of dimenhydrinate in these populations. Administration and Monitoring Administration: Dimenhydrinate is administered orally. Monitoring: There is limited information available regarding monitoring requirements. Overdosage In the event of an overdose, seek medical help immediately or contact a Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. Pharmacology Mechanism of Action: Limited information is available regarding the mechanism of action of dimenhydrinate. Pharmacodynamics and Pharmacokinetics: Limited information is available regarding the pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of dimenhydrinate. Nonclinical Toxicology: Limited information is available regarding nonclinical toxicology. Clinical Studies There is limited information available regarding clinical studies on dimenhydrinate. Storage Store dimenhydrinate at a temperature between 15°C and 30°C (59°F to 86°F). Precautions with Alcohol Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages while using dimenhydrinate.
